titulo: Food and drink: Food and the accusative

aula.objetivo: Order food and drink, use the accusative (der → den, ein → einen), conjugate verbs that change e → i, and use «möchten» with the sentence bracket.

blocos.texto: Lesson goal. By the end of the four sessions, you tell the doer from the receiver of the action, use den, einen and keinen for masculine nouns without hesitating, and replace the object with ihn, sie or es.

blocos.contexto: Camila and Jonas are looking for furniture for her room.

linhas.ru: — Hier ist ein Tisch. Der Tisch ist alt, aber schön.
linhas.pt: — Here's a table. It's old, but nice.
linhas.audio: Hier ist ein Tisch. Der Tisch ist alt, aber schön.

linhas.ru: — Gut, ich kaufe den Tisch. Und ich brauche auch eine Lampe.
linhas.pt: — Great, I'll take the table. And I also need a lamp.
linhas.audio: Gut, ich kaufe den Tisch. Und ich brauche auch eine Lampe.

linhas.ru: — Die Lampe kostet acht Euro. Brauchen Sie auch einen Stuhl?
linhas.pt: — The lamp is eight euros. Do you need a chair too, ma'am?
linhas.audio: Die Lampe kostet acht Euro. Brauchen Sie auch einen Stuhl?

linhas.ru: — Nein danke, ich habe schon einen Stuhl.
linhas.pt: — No, thanks, I already have a chair.
linhas.audio: Nein danke, ich habe schon einen Stuhl.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: German marks the role on the article — but only in the masculine. That's the whole trap: STEP 2: only the masculine changes. So just ask whether the word is a der word. If it isn't, nothing happens.
blocos.comparacao: English works out who does what from word order: "the man sees the dog" and "the dog sees the man" are different because the order changes — "the" never changes. German keeps the order freer and marks the object on the article instead: «Den Hund sieht der Mann» still means "the man sees the dog". You already know the idea from English pronouns: he sees → sees him. German does the same with masculine articles: der → den.

blocos.titulo: The accusative: the direct object changes only in the masculine
blocos.explicacao: German has four cases. For now you need two: the NOMINATIVE (who does the action) and the ACCUSATIVE (the direct object: what you eat, drink, buy or have). The only difference between them is in the MASCULINE singular: der → den, ein → einen, kein → keinen. Feminine, neuter and plural stay the same. Verbs that take the accusative: essen, trinken, kaufen, haben, nehmen, möchten, lesen, sehen.
blocos.comparacao: English "the" never changes: "the cheese" is the same as subject or object. German changes only the masculine: «der Käse» (subject) × «den Käse» (object) — the same switch as he → him.

tabela.exemplo: Ich esse den Käse. Ich trinke einen Saft.

blocos.enunciado: Say: «Ich esse den Käse. Ich trinke einen Saft. Ich esse die Suppe. Ich esse ein Brot.»
